TITLE: Unified Multimodal Learning with Efficient Zero-Shot Video Generation
PROPOSAL: Investigate a native unified model that utilizes a CLIP-style encoder for understanding and a spatial transformer for generating videos from text, via a novel loss function that relieves the pressure of generating consistent features over time and allocates the task-dependent spatial allocation requirements to decoder's attention dynamics.

TITLE: Learning from Web-Crawled Videos without Massive Text Corpora
PROPOSAL: Refine the method in experiment 5 by incorporating a self-supervised visual pre-training stage that leverages web-crawled videos with minimal manual annotation, followed by a few-shot fine-tuning to adapt the pre-trained model to the specific visual generation task. TITLE: Multimodal Adversarial Training for Robust Visual Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a multimodal adversarial training framework for the unified multimodal models, which injects structured noise and perturbations into both text and visual modalities during training to improve the model's robustness against various types of visual and textual corruptions, adversarial attacks, and domain shifts. This framework is designed to promote the model's ability to generate high-quality videos in diverse and challenging scenarios.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the framework on a suite of robustness benchmarks, including data corruption, adversarial attacks, and domain adaptation, and compare to state-of-the-art robustness techniques.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The multimodal adversarial training framework will significantly improve the model's robustness against various types of visual and textual corruptions and domain shifts, enabling it to generate high-quality videos in diverse and challenging scenarios.

PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the sensitivity of unified multimodal models to variations in text, images, and videos, as well as to the hyperparameters and architecture of the model. This framework will enable a detailed understanding of the model's strengths and weaknesses, and facilitate the identification of potential areas for improvement.
CONTROLS: Use a variety of evaluation metrics and visualization techniques, including partial dependence plots, feature importance, and sensitivity analysis, to provide insight into the behavior of the model.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The evaluation framework will provide valuable insights into the sensitivity and robustness of unified multimodal models, enabling researchers and practitioners to design and develop more effective and efficient multimodal systems.

TITLE: Investigating native unified multimodal models with decoupled representations for understanding and generation
PROPOSAL: We experiment with a native unified multimodal model that uses a CLIP-style encoder for visual understanding, a variational autoencoder for visual generation, and a modular architecture to connect them. We evaluate on various tasks, such as text-to-image generation, visual question answering, and OCR, using datasets like LAION-400M, VQA2.0, and SVT.
CONTROLS: We compare our model to existing unified models (Chameleon, Transfusion) and ablate the different components of our model (e.g., CLIP-style encoder vs. vision transformer encoder).
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our model to perform competitively with the existing models on visual understanding tasks, and to outperform them on visual generation tasks. However, the model's performance may degrade on tasks that require fine-grained visual details, such as OCR.

Given the emphasis on theoretical results in some parts of the paper, I've added a mostly experimental proposal to establish a baseline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extending unified multimodal models for video understanding and generation
PROPOSAL: We extend the native unified multimodal model from experiment 1 to incorporate a video encoder for video understanding and a 3D variational autoencoder for video generation. We also add a temporal attention mechanism to handle video temporal dependencies.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the extended model on video understanding tasks like action recognition and video captioning, and ablate the temporal attention mechanism and video encoder architecture.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the extended model will outperform the original model on video understanding tasks, but may experience decreased performance on tasks that require fine-grained spatial visual details, such as object detection.

This proposal extends the model to handle more complex video tasks, an important step towards achieving multimodal understanding and generation across multiple modalities.

We evaluate on various tasks, such as text-to-image generation, visual question answering, and OCR, using datasets like LAION-400M, VQA2.0, and SVT.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised model to the original model and ablate the learnable alignment mechanism, as well as the CLIP-style encoder vs. vision transformer encoder.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our revised model to outperform the original model on various visual generation tasks and possibly on tasks that require fine-grained visual details, such as OCR.

By revising the first experiment, we are refining our initial approach and making it more competitive with state-of-the-art models.

TITLE: Efficient training of pre-trained language models for visual generation
PROPOSAL: We propose an efficient training procedure to add visual generation capabilities to a pre-trained language model without requiring a massive text corpus. Our approach adapts the knowledge distillation framework to align the pre-trained language model with a smaller, multimodal model. We evaluate on text-to-image generation and visual question answering tasks, using datasets like LAMA and VQA2.0.
CONTROLS: We compare our method to a baseline approach of fine-tuning the pre-trained language model from scratch on the multimodal task, and ablate the knowledge distillation objective and temperature parameter.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our method will significantly reduce the need for a large text corpus during the training process, while maintaining or even increasing the model's performance on visual generation tasks.

This new proposal addresses the second open problem in the paper, focusing on efficient training procedures for visual generation in language models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of multimodal pre-training objectives for unified multimodal models
PROPOSAL: We conduct a theoretical analysis on the multimodal pre-training objectives commonly used for unified multimodal models, including autoencoding, adversarial training, and masked language modeling. We derive a set of conditions under which these objectives promote the development of multimodal understanding and generation capabilities.
CONTROLS: We analyze the properties of each objective and compare their performance on various multimodal tasks using synthetic or simulated data.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our analysis to provide insights into the relative importance of each objective and to shed light on the role of pre-training mechanisms in shaping the multimodal behavior of unified models.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Analysis of multimodal pre-training objectives for unified multimodal models
PROPOSAL: We revise our previous proposal to focus on a specific regime - low-data regimes - and derive a set of conditions under which multimodal pre-training objectives promote the development of multimodal understanding and generation capabilities in such regimes. We compare the performance of objectives in synthetic experiments with realistic low-data settings.
CONTROLS: We analyze the properties of each objective and compare their performance in low-data regimes using synthetic data and strong baselines.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our revised analysis to provide deeper insights into how pre-training objectives interact with low-data regimes and to identify the most promising objective for use in such scenarios.

This revised proposal aligns with the paper's focus on practical implications and real-world scenarios, making it more relevant to the experimental domains listed in the paper.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation study on the effects of multimodal pre-training objectives on generalization and robustness
PROPOSAL: We conduct an ablation study to investigate the effects of multimodal pre-training objectives (autoencoding, adversarial training, masked language modeling) on the generalization and robustness of unified multimodal models in text-to-image generation and video understanding tasks, using datasets like ImageNet and LAION.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of different objectives and examine how they affect the model's performance when faced with different levels of data noise, perturbations, and out-of-distribution tasks.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our ablation study will provide insights into the impact of pre-training objectives on the robustness and generalization of unified models, helping identify the most suitable objective for real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the role of adversarial regularizers on unified multimodal models
PROPOSAL: We propose a new approach that employs a combination of adversarial regularizers and landmark-based objectives to improve the robustness and generalization of unified multimodal models. We evaluate our approach on various tasks, including text-to-image generation, video understanding, and visual question answering, using datasets like ImageNet, LAION, and VQA2.0.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to state-of-the-art models and ablate the effects of different types of adversarial regularizers and landmark-based objectives.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to outperform state-of-the-art models on various multimodal tasks, especially in scenarios with high levels of noise, perturbations, or out-of-distribution data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Case studies on unified multimodal models for real-world applications
PROPOSAL: We apply the unified multimodal models developed in previous experiments to real-world applications, such as visual storytelling and multimedia summarization, and evaluate their performance on benchmark datasets like VIST and MSVD.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of different unified models and ablate the effects of different components, such as the type of visual stream and the level of regularization.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours + human annotation costs
PREDICTION: We expect our case studies to provide insights into the practical applications and limitations of unified multimodal models and to highlight potential areas for future research.

This final proposal provides a systematic evaluation of the unified multimodal models in real-world scenarios, complementing the experimental and theoretical results obtained in previous proposals.
